RoomType.maps_to: sts2_rl/rooms.py:_overgrowth_rooms normal_keys ("overgrowth_crawlers" is in normal_keys, never in weak/elite/boss)

Tags.note: OvergrowthCrawlers.Tags = [EncounterTag.Shrinker, EncounterTag.Crawler]; rooms.py's tuple carries the same two values. Order is not observable — the picker only intersects sets (seam/rooms_and_map owns AddWithoutRepeatingTags).

AllPossibleMonsters.maps_to: none -- the sim has no per-encounter monster-preview member
AllPossibleMonsters.rationale: Checked both C# consumers: full_env.py's MONSTER_IDS / _monster_classes() function builds ONE global vocabulary by walking every Monster subclass, a strict superset of any single encounter's roster, so no observation consumer needs a per-encounter preview; EncounterModel.GetAssetPaths (asset preloading), the other consumer, has no sim counterpart at all (headless, no asset streaming). Cost: zero, by enumeration of both consumers. This shape recurs identically across all 85 sim encounters -- see batch report.

GenerateMonsters.maps_to: sts2_rl/monsters/base.py:Encounter.create_monsters (no override) -> [cls(hooks, rng) for cls in monster_classes]; overgrowth_crawlers.py's OVERGROWTH_CRAWLERS_NORMAL = Encounter(id="overgrowth_crawlers_normal", monster_classes=[ShrinkerBeetle, FuzzyWurmCrawler])
GenerateMonsters.note: C# GenerateMonsters returns exactly [(ShrinkerBeetle, null), (FuzzyWurmCrawler, null)] -- a fixed 2-monster roster in that order, zero base.Rng draws. The sim's plain Encounter.create_monsters instantiates monster_classes in list order with no RNG draw, and monster_slots defaults to () so both get slot_name=None, matching null/null. Roster, order, slot names and draw count (0) all match.

ShouldReceiveCombatHooks.maps_to: structural: CombatState.__init__ (sts2_rl/combat.py) only ever calls encounter.create_monsters(); no hooks.register(encounter) call exists anywhere in the codebase
ShouldReceiveCombatHooks.note: EncounterModel.ShouldReceiveCombatHooks => false means an encounter is never itself a hook listener. The sim's Encounter is a plain dataclass never added to HookSystem at all, so the same effect holds by construction.

IsWeak.note: No override in C# (default false); the sim never places this id in any act's weak_keys bucket.

ShouldGiveRewards.maps_to: sts2_rl/monsters/base.py:Encounter.should_give_rewards (default True); consumed by RunDriver._run_combat in driver.py and by the conformance runner's _run_combat in conformance/runner.py
ShouldGiveRewards.note: No override in C# (default true); OVERGROWTH_CRAWLERS_NORMAL does not pass should_give_rewards, so it keeps the dataclass default True.

MinGoldReward.maps_to: sts2_rl/rewards.py:GOLD_REWARD_RANGES[RoomType.MONSTER] = (10, 20), reached via roll_gold_reward's gold_range=None fallback (Encounter.min_gold defaults None)
MinGoldReward.note: No override in C#; base ladder for RoomType.Monster is 10. Ascension Poverty's multiplier (EncounterModel.cs:75-77) is out of scope per PROMPT.md and is not applied anywhere in rewards.roll_gold_reward -- noted, not filed.

MaxGoldReward.note: No override in C#; base ladder for RoomType.Monster is 20 (same Poverty-multiplier note as MinGoldReward).
